bib.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models

question: Can one reinforcement learning algorithm with a single fixed hyperparameter configuration match or beat tuned specialist algorithms across many different domains, including collecting diamonds in Minecraft from scratch?
hypothesis: A world-model agent with robustness techniques (symlog, free bits and KL balancing, percentile return normalization, twohot regression) can learn across domains without retuning.
contributions: DreamerV3, a general algorithm with fixed hyperparameters that outperforms specialized methods across over 150 tasks
First algorithm to collect diamonds in Minecraft from scratch without human data or curricula
Robustness techniques: symlog, symexp twohot, KL balance with free bits, return normalization, 1% unimix
Scaling analysis: robust learning from 12M to 400M parameters and across replay ratios

method.summary: DreamerV3 learns an RSSM world model from replayed experience and trains an actor and critic purely on imagined latent trajectories of the model; actions at environment time are sampled from the actor with no lookahead planning. One hyperparameter table is used across 8 benchmarks; compared against a tuned PPO with fixed hyperparameters and published expert results, plus tuned IMPALA and Rainbow on Minecraft.

datasets.size: 100M env steps; baselines up to 1B and 10B

datasets.size: 100M env steps, episodes up to 36000 steps

datasets.size: up to 40M and 200M env steps (read from Fig 6)

models.name: DreamerV3
models.params: 12M, 25M, 50M, 100M, 200M, 400M (200M default; 12M on the two control suites)
models.architecture: RSSM world model (GRU sequence model with 8 block-diagonal blocks, discrete categorical latents, CNN/MLP encoder and decoder), 3-layer MLP actor and critic, 1-layer MLP reward and continue predictors
models.layers: actor, critic, encoder, decoder MLPs: 3 layers; reward and continue: 1 layer

other.hyperparameters: Table 1: obs and reward normalization yes, reward clip 10 stddev, epoch batch 64x256, 3 epochs, minibatch 8, minibatch length 256, policy trust region 0.2, entropy 0.01, discount 0.997, GAE lambda 0.95, lr 3e-4, grad clip 0.5, Adam eps 1e-5

other.tuned: learning rate and entropy regularizers (values not given)

models.name: Published expert baselines (MuZero, Rainbow, IQN, PPG, IMPALA, R2D2+, SPR, IRIS, TWM, SimPLe, EfficientZero, D4PG, DMPO, MPO, DrQ-v2, CURL, Boot DQN)

training.objective: World model: L = E[sum_t (1*L_pred + 1*L_dyn + 0.1*L_rep)] with symlog squared loss for decoder, symexp twohot for reward, logistic regression for continue, KL with free bits 1 nat; critic: maximum likelihood of lambda-returns (categorical, twohot) plus 0.3-weighted replay loss; actor: Reinforce surrogate with percentile return normalization and entropy 3e-4
training.optimizer: LaProp (eps 1e-20, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.99) with Adaptive Gradient Clipping AGC(0.3, eps 1e-3)
training.steps: Per benchmark env steps (Table 2): Minecraft 100M, DMLab 100M, ProcGen 50M, Atari 200M, Atari100K 400K, Proprio 500K, Visual 1M
training.seq_len: 64 (batch length); imagination horizon 15 (Table 4), text says prediction horizon T = 16
training.regularisation: 1% unimix on categoricals, free nats 1, critic EMA regularizer (scale 1, decay 0.98), zero-initialised output layers of reward predictor and critic; no prioritized replay
training.compute: GPU days by benchmark (Table 2): Minecraft 8.9, DMLab 2.9, ProcGen 16.1, Atari 7.7, Atari100K 0.1, BSuite 0.5, Proprio 0.3, Visual 0.1
training.seeds: 5 per benchmark for Dreamer and PPO; 1 for ProcGen; 10 for BSuite; 10 for Minecraft

other.replay: uniform buffer with online queue; latent states stored and written back
other.replay_ratio_per_benchmark: Minecraft 32, DMLab 32, ProcGen 64, Atari 32, Atari100K 128, BSuite 1024, Proprio 512, Visual 512
other.action_repeat: Minecraft 1, DMLab 4, ProcGen 1, Atari 4, Atari100K 4, BSuite 1, Proprio 2, Visual 2
other.gradient_steps_example: replay ratio 32 on Atari with action repeat 4 and batch 16x64 = 1 gradient step per 128 env steps, 1.5M steps over 200M env steps

inference.decoding: sample actions from the actor policy, no lookahead planning

results.quote: over the course of training, 100% of Dreamer agents obtain one or more diamonds regardless of episode boundaries, compared to 0% of the baseline agents.

limits: Authors concede diamonds appear in only 0.4% of episodes at the 100M budget.
Model size (200M or 12M) and replay ratio vary by benchmark (Table 2), so 'fixed' refers to Table 4 hyperparameters only.
EfficientZero holds the Atari100k state of the art (gamer mean 190 vs 125) but uses online search and early resets, so the authors call comparison difficult.
DMLab baselines are compared at 1B steps against Dreamer at 100M, because 10B runs were infeasible.
ProcGen used 1 seed; Dreamer scores 0.01 on BSuite exploration versus 0.68 for Boot DQN.
Minecraft environment was modified from MineRL (early-termination removed, jump held 200ms) and evaluation protocol was set by the authors.
All experiments are simulators or games; none involve language models.
Text gives prediction horizon T=16 while Table 4 lists imagination horizon H=15.

terms.definition: symlog(x) = sign(x) ln(|x|+1), with symexp as inverse; a bi-symmetric log transform for targets and inputs of unknown scale
network outputs logits over exponentially spaced bins B = symexp(-20..+20) and trains on twohot targets with cross entropy
clipping the dynamics and representation losses below 1 nat
fraction of time steps trained on per time step collected from the environment, without action repeat
